title: In-Gen. Bring your own AI agent Dev Studio.
author: Kingnorik
selftext:
Hi guys. I present to you my game engine, In-Gen, that's sorta like a dev studio now I suppose. I made it so as to have a framework for all my products to be made in, and then I was like might as well release it. Especially after seeing so many posts of people making games not even using a CLI. It's free, runs on your computer like a standard game engine. It's basically a CLI integrated into a scene editor. But you can also work through MCP as well. You have full control of the games when it comes to sculpting the scene, importing assets, placements etc. What you can't do is get stuff to move without AI. This engine isn't meant for one shots, but you certainly can, as the video above shows. It's meant for iterations. So after your one shot the engine already has your assets registered and built out systems you can edit in plain data in between resets. In that regard the AI agents also function cheaper and better here than in normal convos thanks to a NCM approach I took we call Harmony Intent, you can read the tech info below.   
  
We also have some nice debugging features, best one is Watch Me Play. It records you playing in editor and then sends it directly to the AI to review and debug. I also added some crazy new feature called Director which allows the AI to easily make cutscenes for your games or even shorts and movies one day. Again everything is free, no signing up, just download. Eventually, maybe next week after my usage resets I'll get the publish feature working and you guys can publish your creations directly to the site. Also working on android and IOS publishing. The engine has no royalties or anything monetary. 

Read enough? Then visit the site for a cool flying simulator look at foliage, water, and sunlight and bloom that everyone just loves. Also have 3 games and the one shot demo. Tome Knight is my "dream game". Will be a full steam release.  First zone is avail. It's Skyrim meets pokemon meets palworld. Districts is basically the full game will be on mobile soon. I love city sims and wanted to make something that looks cozy, but isn't. Legends and Loot is my android game that I'm remaking in the engine, going for 2.5D.   
[Website](http://gengaming.net)

About me: 39 year old married dad, work in banking. Went to school about 20 years ago for game dev. Had to quit due to the 2008 financial crisis and get a real job. Started making Tome Knight in unreal around 2021 due to COVID allowing me to work from home. Been making it in my spare time, got about to where I am now story wise, but it's just too much for one person. Started the hobby again when AI got good.

 And now here is AI for the tech stuff.

\*\*What In-gen is, technically\*\*



In-gen is a Windows game editor with an AI agent harness, Harmony, built into it. It's in free public beta and updates itself.



\- \*\*Engine:\*\* three.js r187 (WebGPU + WebGL2), Rapier physics, Recast navigation, meshoptimizer LODs, KTX2 textures, WebRTC multiplayer, inside an Electron 43 shell.

\- \*\*Four layers:\*\* Kernel (rendering, physics, world), Runtime (input, UI, scenes), Authoring (the editor) and Game (your rules). A shipped game never depends on editor code.

\- \*\*Output:\*\* a standalone Windows game or a browser build. Release builds strip editor notes, pack game data into encrypted packs and ship with a Content Security Policy.



\*\*Bring your own AI\*\*



Harmony works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Antigravity, on your own subscription or API key. You can also drive In-gen from Claude Code or Codex over MCP. Outside agents only connect when you turn that on, and every change shows up as an approval card in the editor.



\*\*Game rules you can tune yourself\*\*



When Harmony builds a mechanic, it doesn't bury the numbers in code. Each rule becomes a System with a plain-language description, and its tuning lives in typed spreadsheet-style Sheets. For example, a Coin Pickup System reads a Coins sheet with a Gold column. After that, you change Gold yourself, with no new prompt and no token cost.



\*\*Harmony Intent: making the agent cheaper\*\*



Most of an agent's cost isn't the code it writes. It's re-reading context on every tool call. So Harmony works in a compact language we call Harmony Intent:



\- It reads a scene as one short line per object, about 3.8x fewer tokens than the scene JSON.

\- It applies a whole batch of edits as one step, with one approval and one undo.



On our scene-editing benchmark (7 tasks, each run twice):



\- Average cost per task dropped from \~89k to \~34k tokens (about 60% less).

\- Tool calls dropped from 12.9 to 4.7 per task.

\- Success went from 11/14 to 14/14.

\- Placing 34 trees went from 235k tokens to 44k.



It's a small benchmark, but the direction was consistent.



The same idea applies to 3D models. Harmony writes a short Intent plan, and Kiln (a code-to-mesh tool that ships inside In-gen) builds it into a GLB locally, with no credits. In two head-to-head tests, plans cost 13% and 32% less than having the agent write raw Kiln JavaScript.



\*\*CineGen Director: cutscenes and films\*\*



Cutscenes are written in Harmony Flow, a plain-text shot language: cameras, framing, character actions, lighting, fades and sound cues. The same cut plays as an in-game cutscene or renders frame by frame to MP4. Frame-stepped rendering means no dropped frames or load hitches baked into the video, and re-rendering a single shot only redraws the frames that changed.



The 60-second short "From Idea to Asset" was made this way:



\- The main film is a \~290-line Flow script, plus a 46-line one for the two reuse scenes at the end.

\- The robot, the maker and the hologram are real reusable 3D assets built with Kiln, each with its own animation clips. That's why the same robot can walk into a different scene unchanged.

\- The music and sound effects were generated locally with Stable Audio 3.



The "Made with In-gen" intro every game opens with was also directed in CineGen.



\*\*Other tools it sets up for you\*\*



\- A private copy of Blender 4.5(optional install) that Harmony drives in the background for remeshing, UV unwrapping, baking and rig weights.

\- Local sound and music generation with Stable Audio 3.

\- Create Tree for instanced trees.

\- Tiling PBR materials from a prompt or a photo.

\- Meshy as an option with your own account.



\*\*An honest comparison\*\*



I built the same zombie game, DEAD HOUSE, twice from one prompt: once with plain Claude Code straight to three.js, once inside In-gen.



\- \*\*Cost:\*\* the three.js run used 20% of my 5-hour Claude window, and the In-gen run used 33%. So In-gen is not cheaper per one-shot run today.

\- \*\*What the extra cost buys:\*\* 7 editable Systems with tuning sheets, a scene you can open and rearrange, and iteration without re-prompting. I polished the In-gen version in the editor afterwards (moving furniture, tuning sheets), and that's the version that's playable on Gen Haven.



\*\*Links\*\*



\- In-gen (free beta, Windows): [https://gengaming.net](https://gengaming.net)

\- The CineGen short: [https://youtu.be/JvAbLBQa-CA](https://youtu.be/JvAbLBQa-CA)

\- Games made with it, playable in the browser: [https://gengaming.net/haven/](https://gengaming.net/haven/)

comments.body: Dang, thought you guys would appreciate this. Solves a lot of problems guys post here.
